column28: Resolved by the nasalized-low-vowel adjudication. The former scope tension (R/T pp.150-152 North Sea Germanic vs Fulk §4.11 p.72 Anglo-Frisian) arose from conflating two changes. Old Saxon shares the NASALIZATION of stressed low vowels (R/T §5.1.2 p.142) but not the categorical, systematic ROUNDING: it retains *a-long consistently in the inherited PGmc class and shows variable *a-long/*o-long in the Ingvaeonic class (Campbell §119 p.44; Fulk §4.11 p.72). Nasalization is therefore north_sea_germanic and the rounding SC104 is anglo_frisian.

column28: Campbell sec.417 p.170: "When a consonant follows, xs > s in OE" (waestm, -waesma, North. sesta), and the change "is found in all West Gmc. languages, and in North Gmc." (ON isl, ON nysa, OS weslon, OS wastum, OS niustan, OHG niusen, OS/OHG lastar < *laxstra-). Brunner sec.221.2 p.184 adds that the following consonant may also be *j (neos(i)an, thisl, waesma, waestm, Nhb. sesta) and that x stays in wrixlan, where the l is vocalic. Bulbring sec.527 p.215: "xs vor Konsonanten in der Regel zu s". R/T pp.157-158 give PGmc *niuhsijana > PWGmc *niusjan > OE neosan, *sehsto > Nhb. sesta, *thihslu > OE thisl, (post-)PWGmc *wahstm > OE waestm, and conclude that *h was lost "possibly variably, possibly only in some dialects, when followed by two or more consonants"; they read it as a shared northern WGmc change but allow that the North Germanic agreement is partly parallel drift. NOT Proto-Germanic: Gothic retains the *h (bi-niuhsjan, saihsta). For fist itself the cognate set is West Germanic only (Kroonen p.160 *funhsti-: OE fyst, OHG fust, G Faust, Du. vuist, MDu. vuust; Orel p.157 *funxwstiz adds OFris fest, OS fust); no Gothic or ON reflex of this lexeme is attested, so the stage is set from *niuhsjan/*sehsto/*thihslu, not from fist.

column29: Adjudicated 2026 (sc029-sc030-awj-resolution-and-au-fronting-adjudication.md): verdict RETAIN, no reorder, no rule change, no output change. The executable rule is correct; the description around it was not. 'Glide formation' was a misnomer twice over, since the change is the undoing of a West Germanic gemination and its effect is to make the glide vocalic. Stage preoe and scope english_specific are confirmed (OHG houwi, gistrouwen and OS hoi point to the unresolved West Germanic stage, R/T p.173). Goth. hawi, ON hey), and SC010 gained the *w branch that now supplies the geminate. Both witnesses therefore reach SC029 as *áwwj, and the two singleton branches were removed as unwitnessed; the surviving pair are stress-notation variants, not a historical stress condition. The domain is the *a type only: the *iwj witness hue geminates at SC010 and is correctly not resolved here (Campbell §120.2 p.46). New chronology edge SC010 -> SC029 (feeding). column28: Thorhallsdottir 1993 ch.5 pp.114-137, acquired and READ DIRECTLY (the committed vision transcript in the reference library), previously known only through Ringe-Taylor vol.2 pp.12,151. She rejects an inherited PIE *w and derives the Old English *w as an inner-Germanic phonetic hiatus glide (p.136, after Bremer 1886:72-73, cf. p.120). TWO MECHANISMS: (i) regular phonological insertion, environment strictly _ *u, i.e. 1sg and 1pl pres.ind. *-u and *-um and the reduplicated-preterite plural *-um, *-uth, *-un (pp.120,126,127), and (ii) analogical generalization of that *w through the whole present paradigm and the pret.ptc., assisted by the preterite stem *seuw(un) and by etymological-*w verbs such as OE flowan (p.127), complete by pre-OE (p.128 n.23, p.136). Old Frisian shares the generalized type, OHG and OS *j is a separate later inner-German event (pp.123,130,134,136) - this directly confirms the anglo_frisian scope. WHAT CAPR EXECUTES IS MECHANISM (ii): the OE citation form is the infinitive *saan, whose following vowel is *a, NOT one of the cells that receives *w phonologically, so the *w of sawan is analogical and the Foma environment (*a _ V) is a citation-form proxy for the generalized outcome, not a reconstruction of the phonological conditioning. NO SPLIT: the phonological rule has no witness in a citation-form corpus and would be a dead rule, and the generalization is analogy rather than a sound law. The 'distinct mechanisms stay distinct' policy is discharged by describing them separately here and in the reader chapter. Confidence raised B to A because the sole stated ground of the B - that the phonological-versus-analogical architecture had not been checked against the specialist source - is now discharged. Residual uncertainty recorded separately, NOT folded into the confidence: the executable environment is a proxy, and SC102 before SC101 remains an assertion from Ringe-Taylor p.151 which Thorhallsdottir nowhere supports (ch.5 never discusses *a-fronting). DEFERRED: the Foma identifier EAFHiatusWInsertion now understates the rule and should be renamed under the behaviour-neutral rename protocol in a separate pass. See governing memo sec.13.4.

column29: Split out of SC026/SC027 by the nasal-spirant adjudication; low-vowel branch corrected and rule repositioned by the nasalized-low-vowel adjudication. PGmc *-Nx- > long nasalized vowel + *x, with loss of the nasal (Campbell §119 p.44; Fulk §4.1 p.55; Ringe vol.1 §3.2.7(ii) pp.149-150). Pan-Germanic: Go. theihan, brahta, thuhta; OHG dihan, brahta, fuht, fust; OE theon, brohte, thuhte, fuht. Distinguished from the Ingvaeonic law by the comparative test: here the nasal is lost in ALL daughters, whereas SC026/SC027 witnesses keep it outside Ingvaeonic (OHG fimf, gans, ander, jugund). Only *a, *i, *u occur (Fulk §4.1). The low-vowel branch now outputs nasalized long *a-ogonek-macron (transducer symbol {*a-tilde}), NOT *o-long: the rounding is the later Anglo-Frisian SC104, and Gothic, North Germanic, Old High German and Old Saxon all keep unrounded a (Campbell §119 p.44; Fulk §4.11 p.72). Moved ahead of SC096 and of the daughter-specific NWGmc/PWGmc innovations, so that a pan-Germanic change no longer follows them. Both branches are witnessed: fist *funxstiz > *fuxsti on the high branch, thought *thanxte > *tha-tilde-xte on the low branch; see the generated firing census for the current population.

column9: Anglo-Frisian rounding of the long nasalized low vowel
column25: One later Anglo-Frisian change with three independent feeding sources: SC103 (PGmc *aNx), SC026/SC027 (the North Sea Germanic nasal-spirant law) and SC025 (inherited long *a before a retained nasal). Campbell §128 n.1 p.50 states the unification directly: the change affected the nasalized vowel from PGmc §119 and from Ingvaeonic §121 at the same time. Earlier boundaries are executable feeding dependencies: stating this rule before SC025 or before SC026 strands the nasalized vowel and month, spoon and goose are rejected. No later boundary against SC101 or SC004 is claimed: the input is segmentally nasalized, so the oral *a-long created by SC004 < *ai is simply outside this rule's domain, which is exactly Fulk's observation (§4.1 p.55) that it did not fall together with OE a-long < ai.
column29: Created by the nasalized-low-vowel adjudication, which found that CAPR had telescoped one later change into three earlier rules. Executable {*a-tilde} -> {*o-long}, unconditioned. Confidence A independently of the disputed *e1 reconstruction that feeds SC025: the rounding is evidenced from PGmc *Nx reflexes, from nasal-spirant reflexes, from retained-nasal forms, and by cross-dialect comparison with Gothic, North Germanic, Old High German and Old Saxon a-long (Campbell §119 p.44, §121 p.47, §128 n.1 p.50; Fulk §4.1 p.55, §4.11 p.72; Ringe vol.1 §3.2.7(ii) pp.149-150; R/T §5.1.2 p.142; Brunner §80 Anm.1; Luick §301.1 p.276). Scope anglo_frisian, not north_sea_germanic: Old Saxon shares the nasalization but rounds only variably for the Ingvaeonic class and not at all for the inherited PGmc class. No explicit *i-nasal-long or *u-nasal-long is represented: those develop exactly like oral *i-long and *u-long (Campbell §121 p.47) and no later rule depends on their nasality.
